newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-COWBOYS' STAR IRVIN UNSURE IF HE WILL PLAY IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-COWBOYS' STAR IRVIN UNSURE IF HE WILL PLAY IN 1997.

text.p: Embattled Dallas Cowboys star receiver Michael Irvin said Wednesday he was not sure if he would play football next season -- or ever again.

"I truly don't know what I am going to do," Irvin said at a news conference in which he announced that he was suing Dallas police and a local television station in connection with false sexual assault charges.
"Right now, I just don't have that intensity and emotion about the game," said Irvin, who skipped a Cowboys minicamp this week.

The 31-year-old Irvin, one of the elite players at his position in the NFL and a key member of three Dallas Super Bowl champions, added that he would retire if he could not recover his passion for football.
Irvin has three years left on a five-year contract with Dallas that included a $4.5 million signing bonus.
The Cowboys were 2-3 during Irvin's suspension last season, but went 8-3 when he returned. Despite missing five games, he caught a team-leading 64 passes for 962 yards.

Irvin, who said his family would have the final say in whether or not he returns to play for the Cowboys next season, appeared nostalgic for a time before his recent troubles began when football was the most important thing in his life.
"I want to go back to being that happy man who played the game with intensity," he said.
Dallas signed free agent receiver Anthony Miller Monday with the intention of teaming him with Irvin, but he could end up replacing the star unless Irvin has a change of heart.

Irvin's attorney Peter Ginsberg said the All-Pro wide receiver's civil rights were violated in the police handling of assault allegations by a topless dancer who claimed last December that Irvin held a gun against her head while Dallas teammate Erik Williams raped her.
Both Irvin and Williams were cleared of the allegations after a police investigation revealed that the incident was a fabrication. The dancer, Nina Shahravan, is awaiting trial on perjury charges.
Williams filed lawsuits against the City of Dallas, five police officers and Dallas television station KXAS-TV in February, and Irvin said Wednesday he had joined those suits.
"I am basically tired about some of the things that have been said and I am not running any more, I am not hiding any more," Irvin said.
"I want to get the truth out about everything."
Ginsberg said Dallas police and KXAS-TV jumped to accuse Irvin and Williams and were slow to clear the two men even after seeing firm evidence that they had done no wrong.

Irvin has been under intense scrutiny since pleading no contest to a second-degree felony drug possession last July. He was sentenced to four years probation, 800 hours of community service and fined $10,000.
The NFL then suspended Irvin for the first five games of the 1997 season for conduct detrimental to the league.
Irvin said he has stuck to the terms of his probation, was focusing on his family and had passed numerous drug tests.
Some of Irvin's teammates have urged him to to declare his intentions one way or another, but he said he was still struggling to decide his next step.
"As soon as I know, they'll know," he said.
